subject: Gaps in generated responses - intermittent blank segments
messages:
From: John Dolan <john.dolan@frescoai.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Gaps in generated responses - intermittent blank segments

Hi Sofia,

We've been seeing intermittent gaps in the middle of generated responses from the Redwood API over the last 48 hours. Example: one of our completed responses suddenly has a 3–7 second blank segment where the server appears to stop streaming before resuming. The final output is still delivered, but the UX shows a ~5s freeze (users think the model hung).

What we've captured so far:
- Request ID: r-6a3f9b2c (attached logs)
- Model: redwood/gpt-{{open}}-2b (we pinned this in production)
- Mode: streaming (chunked SSE) with keep-alive on
- Approx timestamps: 2027-06-01T02:42:18Z, 2027-06-01T02:42:23Z (gap observed)
- We attached a screenshot of the client showing the freeze and the raw call logs (call-logs-20270601.json).

This affects about 3% of sessions for one of our high-latency customers. Can you confirm whether anything on the Redwood side could cause intermittent blank segments in the middle of a stream?

Thanks,
John
John Dolan
Head of Platform
FrescoAI

Attachments: screenshot-1.png (image), call-logs-20270601.json (text)

Also, if you can share one raw streaming payload (the exact bytes) that would be ideal. If you're not able to share raw payloads, the request ids and the attached call-logs are helpful.

I'll come back with findings within 24 hours, or sooner if we see something obvious.

Subject: Fw: Gaps in generated responses - FrescoAI (request id r-6a3f9b2c)

Folks — forwarding Fresco's report. Key context: streaming SSE session with a noticeable 3–7s blank interval in the UI while the final completion still arrives. They saw ~3% of sessions affected for one customer. Attached are their call logs (call-logs-20270601.json).

Please prioritize the following checks:
- Search platform logs for request id r-6a3f9b2c and adjacent calls for any re-transmits, stream resets, or partial chunk drops.
- Confirm whether we observed any connection-level resets or TCP retransmits at the edge at those timestamps.
- Check the streaming runtime traces for any pauses in the token flush path or KV-cache stalls.
- If we can't reproduce, advise on recommended customer-side checks (SDK versions, parsers, proxy timeouts).

I'm attaching our collected traces (call-id-logs.zip). Will update John once we have something.

Thanks,
Sofia
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, runtime-engineering@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fw: Gaps in generated responses - FrescoAI (r-6a3f9b2c)

Quick update from runtime triage. We pulled traces for r-6a3f9b2c and several neighboring calls (logs attached: runtime-trace-20270602.json). Findings so far:

- Platform traces show a continuous token stream being emitted from the runtime. There are no pauses or RT-level backpressure events logged in that request's path.
- Edge logs show a clean TCP session; no resets or retransmits correlated to the observed timestamp.
- Token counts and final output match what Fresco posted in their call-logs. We do not see missing tokens on the server side.

Hypothesis: client-side SSE / stream parser behavior. We have seen instances where older client SDKs (v1.3.0 and earlier) that use a custom line-buffered SSE parser can drop an empty chunk boundary if the application strips leading newlines when concatenating chunks. This presents to users as a momentary freeze even though the server kept streaming.

Action items for Fresco (suggested to send to customer):
- Confirm client SDK version and whether you use a custom SSE parser. If v1.3.0 or earlier, upgrade to v1.3.2 (patch released 2027-05-20) which fixes chunk boundary handling.
- If possible, capture the raw streaming socket (tcpdump) for one of the affected sessions and share it with us.
- As a quick workaround, enable a short client-side keepalive/timer to surface partial chunks instead of waiting for chunk finalization.

If you want, we can run a joint debugging session (remote screenshare) to capture a raw stream. From the infra side, there is no platform evidence of a server-side gap at the reported timestamps.

-Michael
Senior SRE, Runtime
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: John Dolan <john.dolan@frescoai.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Gaps in generated responses - intermittent blank segments

Hi John — quick update from our runtime team: we reviewed the request traces and did not find any server-side pauses or network resets for the request ids you supplied (see attached trace). Our current hypothesis is that the gap is happening on the client side during SSE chunk parsing.

Recommended next steps:
- Please confirm your Redwood SDK version and whether you're using a custom SSE parser. If you're on v1.3.0 or older, please upgrade to v1.3.2.
- If you can reproduce, capture the raw streaming payload (tcpdump) and share it with us — we'll analyze it together.
- As a temporary mitigation, consider enabling a local UI heartbeat that shows partial data as it's received rather than waiting for chunk completion.

We're marking this as "no platform evidence" for now. If you can provide raw socket captures or you continue to see the issue after upgrading, we'll reopen and continue triage.

Regards,
Sofia
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

Attachments: runtime-trace-20270602.json
From: John Dolan <john.dolan@frescoai.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Gaps in generated responses - intermittent blank segments

Thanks, Sofia and team. We upgraded our SDK to v1.3.2 yesterday and pushed a small change to our SSE parser to avoid stripping leading newlines. We've run for 24 hours on the affected traffic slice and haven't observed the freeze again. We'll capture a raw stream if the problem reoccurs and will re-open the ticket. Appreciate the quick triage and the suggested steps.

Best,
John
